title: A Giant Planet Vanished — and Won't Be Back for Decades
summary:
For the first time, astronomers watched a giant planet vanish. The 'hot Jupiter' called TOI-2535 b sits about 1,000 light-years from Earth, but it wobbled out of view instead of crossing its star.

Astronomers first spotted it in April 2019 using NASA's TESS telescope, which finds planets by watching for tiny dips in a star's brightness. TOI-2535 b is a gas giant like Jupiter, but it circles its star in 8.25 days — Mercury takes 88 days.

Over seven years, researchers noticed its crossings arrived as much as six hours earlier or later than predicted. Then, in March, the planet simply did not show up at all.

Researchers believe a neighboring giant planet with a tilted orbit is tugging on it, tipping it out of line with Earth. Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, called it the most extreme example researchers have seen.

The moon's tilted orbit works the same way, which is why we do not see an eclipse every month. TOI-2535 b will not cross its star again for another 30 to 50 years.
why_it_matters: Watching a planet vanish teaches you that space is always moving and changing, and that careful watching can reveal things no one has ever seen before.

keywords.explanation: Astronomers are scientists who study the stars, planets, and everything in space.
A hot Jupiter is a giant planet like Jupiter that sits very close to its star, so it is very hot.
A gas giant is a huge planet made mostly of gas, like Jupiter.
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, used to measure how far away stars are.
An eclipse happens when one thing in space passes in front of another and blocks its light.

background_read: A telescope in space can find planets around other stars by watching for a tiny dip in a star's light when a planet crosses in front of it.
Planets circle their stars in a steady path, so scientists can predict when each crossing should happen.
If a nearby planet pulls on it, the crossing can shift or stop lining up with Earth, so the planet seems to vanish.
